Nasir Khusraw was a Persian poet, traveller and Ismaili thinker, born in 1004 at Qubadiyan, now in Tajikistan, who spent his last decades in exile at Yamgan in Badakhshan, Afghanistan.

He was a tax official under the Seljuks when, in about 1045, he set out on a seven-year journey to Mecca and to Cairo, capital of the Fatimid caliphs. His travel book, the Safarnama, is a vivid source on the cities he saw. In Cairo he became an Ismaili missionary.

Back in Khorasan he was hunted as a heretic and fled to the mountains of Badakhshan, where he wrote poetry and philosophy and won the region to Ismaili Islam. The Ismailis of Badakhshan and the Pamirs in Afghanistan and Tajikistan, who now follow the Aga Khan, still revere him as their founder. He is counted among the great poets of Persian, with Rudaki before him.
sum: Nasir Khusraw was a Persian poet, traveller and Ismaili thinker, born in 1004 at Qubadiyan, now in Tajikistan, who spent his last decades in exile at Yamgan in Badakhshan, Afghanistan.
